comments.text: Maths! It is expected that mathematics will be dominated by AI as one of the first topics. Some experiments showed, that it's still a long way. I created a custom GPT "Math Formal Proof Assistant" that is able to communicate with a formal proof assistant runtime (Coq in this case) very similar to the built-in python code interpreter. As of now it is able to automatically proof simple things like "forall a, b:nat, a+b = b+a". But I have no idea how to make money with this 🙂 [The ID is "g-apmVjO2Ea-math-formal-proof-assistant"; not allowed to post the complete link here.]

comments.author: @TemNoon
comments.text: Thank you for your videos. Good content, interesting analysis, little fluff. I've developed 7 GPTs in total, but 3 of them I decided to put in the store. Something you didn't mention was creating a page on the website that was registered with your profile, which I have now done on my site, with a "GPTs" menu to easily get to the "home page" of these GPTs, that includes features, instructions, and a GPT "Caveat". Something that you haven't mentioned which I just confirmed for sure is that in your "explore" screen when you look at the GPTs you've used along with the GPTs you've built, there is a number of Chats that the GPT has been used in. That is a global number, so I know about 10 people have used my most popular GPT since last night, since I haven't (unless just opening the GPT without initiating a chat adds one to that number. Hmm. I'll have to try that out). All of the GPTs I've set up for the store and given a GPT page (on temnoon.com) I created because I wanted to use them. Journal Recognizer OCR is that most popular one, currently with 363 chat. In know I'm not the only OCR app out there, but I tried out a bunch of them, and many of them couldn't even handle pages that my JR-OCR does a great job on. In researching OCRwith GPT-4V (including creating an Assisant API app, that worked practically identically to the ChatGPT interface) I noticed that when the Code Interpreter is included in the GPT, it does WAY WORSE at OCR, at least for handwriting. Many times on the same image, turning on the Code Interpreter (checkin thte box in the GPT builder) will significantly degrade performance. This should be researched further, to see when the Code Interpreter helps, and when it hurts. I've done some brief publicity on Reddit and Discord (on OpenAI channels and subs) but it's been quite a challenge. OpenAI always seems to do major things on Wednesday, so I'm expecting the store to hit tomorrow. If you have a moment, give it a try with any kind of handwriting, or better would be a notebook page that has writing and drawings. That is my target use case. https://chat.openai.com/g/g-T7bW2qVzx-journal-recognizer-ocr
